questions.text: How often do you do resistance or strength training (weights, resistance bands, bodyweight exercises)?

responses.label: Never / less than once a month

triggers.if_response: Never / less than once a month

questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; Wolff's law (bone loading); ACSM resistance training guidelines

questions.text: On a typical weekday, how many hours do you spend sitting or lying down (excluding sleep)?
questions.source: Biswas et al. 2015 (Ann Intern Med); OMICS back-pain assessment

questions.text: How would you describe your daily protein intake (meat, fish, eggs, legumes, dairy, protein shakes)?

responses.label: Very low — mostly plant carbs, little protein
Low — some protein daily but less than 0.8 g/kg

questions.source: Bauer et al. 2013 (ESPEN protein guidelines for elderly); OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: How much calcium-rich food do you eat (dairy, fortified plant milks, tinned fish with bones, leafy greens)?

responses.label: Rarely / none — no dairy or calcium-fortified foods
Low — 1 serving per day or less

questions.source: IOF calcium intake guidelines; OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: How much outdoor sun exposure do you typically get, and do you take a vitamin D supplement?

responses.label: Little sun but take vitamin D supplement
Plenty of sun and/or supplement daily

questions.source: NICE NG187 vitamin D; Holick 2007 (NEJM); OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: Have you ever had a bone fracture as an adult (age 18+), including stress fractures?
questions.source: FRAX tool (WHO fracture risk); OMICS back-pain assessment

questions.text: Which bone(s) were fractured? (select all that apply)
questions.source: FRAX tool fracture site risk weighting; NOF guidelines

questions.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with osteoporosis or osteopenia (low bone density), confirmed by DEXA scan or doctor?
questions.source: WHO osteoporosis T-score criteria; OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: Did you experience menopause before age 45 (natural or surgical), or are you currently perimenopausal or postmenopausal?
questions.source: IOF SCOPE (premature ovarian insufficiency and bone loss); Stevenson 1990

questions.text: Have you used oral or injectable corticosteroids (prednisone, hydrocortisone, dexamethasone) for more than 3 months?

responses.label: Yes — short course only (<3 months cumulative)
Yes — more than 12 months or currently taking

questions.source: ACR glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis guidelines; OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: Have you ever had a significantly low body weight (BMI below 18.5) for 6 months or more, or a history of restrictive eating?

responses.label: Yes — prolonged or with eating disorder history

questions.source: FRAX low BMI risk; Golden 2003 (anorexia and bone density)

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with any form of arthritis (osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, or other)?
questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; ACR osteoarthritis guidelines

questions.text: Do you have persistent joint pain or stiffness? If yes, which area(s) are affected? (select all)
questions.source: OMICS back-pain assessment; Woolf and Pfleger 2003 (global burden musculoskeletal)

questions.text: How long have you had lower back pain?
questions.source: NICE NG59 low back pain; OMICS back-pain assessment

questions.text: If you work at a desk, how would you describe your workstation ergonomics?

responses.label: Ergonomic setup — monitor at eye level, supportive chair
Mixed — some adjustments but not optimal
Unadjusted / poor setup — slouched, screen too low
Laptop on sofa / bed / floor regularly

questions.source: OMICS back-pain assessment; Hartvigsen et al. 2018 (Lancet back pain series)

questions.text: Does your work involve heavy lifting, repetitive bending, or sustained awkward postures?

responses.label: Moderate — regular lifting 10–25 kg or repetitive bending
Heavy — frequent lifting >25 kg or sustained awkward posture

questions.source: OMICS back-pain assessment; Punnett & Wegman 2004 (Scand J Work Environ Health)

questions.text: Do you work or spend extended time in cold environments (outdoors in winter, cold storage, refrigeration)?
questions.source: OMICS back-pain assessment; Ljungberg et al. 1999 (Scand J Work Environ Health)

questions.text: How many times have you fallen (lost your balance and hit the ground) in the past 12 months?
questions.source: AGS/BGS falls prevention guidelines; FRAX falls input

questions.text: Do you have difficulty with either of the following: (a) opening jars or gripping objects firmly, (b) climbing a flight of stairs without resting?
questions.source: EWGSOP2 sarcopenia criteria (grip strength proxy); Fried frailty phenotype

questions.text: Have you had a significant musculoskeletal injury (joint dislocation, ligament tear, tendon rupture, disc prolapse) in the past?
questions.source: OMICS back-pain assessment; Magnusson & Kjaer 2003 (Achilles tendon review)

questions.text: Regarding your Achilles / heel pain: when does the pain occur?
questions.source: VISA-A questionnaire (Achilles tendinopathy); OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: Do you experience neck stiffness, headaches at the base of the skull, or rounded-shoulder discomfort at the end of the workday?

responses.label: Daily and persistent into the evening

questions.source: OMICS back-pain assessment; Szeto et al. 2002 (neck/shoulder in VDT workers)

questions.text: How often do you feel physically exhausted after activities that would not have tired you a year ago?
questions.source: Fried frailty phenotype (exhaustion criterion); EWGSOP2 sarcopenia staging

questions.text: Have you unintentionally lost more than 5% of your body weight in the past 6 months?
questions.source: Fried frailty phenotype (weight loss criterion); MNA screening tool

questions.text: Compared to peers your age, how would you rate your walking speed over a short distance (e.g., crossing a road)?

responses.label: About the same as most peers
Much slower / need aid to walk

questions.source: EWGSOP2 gait speed criterion; Fried frailty phenotype

questions.text: Where do you notice most of your excess body fat?
questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; Visser et al. (sarcopenic obesity and bone); Diabetes UK waist guidelines

questions.text: Do you specifically practise balance or proprioception exercises (yoga, tai chi, single-leg stands, balance boards)?
questions.source: Cochrane review (Sherrington 2017 — exercise for falls prevention)

questions.text: Are you currently taking or have you taken hormone replacement therapy (HRT / MHT — estrogen ± progesterone)?

responses.label: Took HRT in the past — now stopped

questions.source: NICE NG187 menopause; WHI bone density outcomes; IOF HRT and osteoporosis

questions.text: How would you rate your overall flexibility and joint mobility (ability to touch toes, full shoulder reach, hip mobility)?

responses.label: Very flexible — full range of motion, no stiffness
Limited — noticeable restrictions affecting daily tasks

questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; ACSM flexibility guidelines
